summary.text: Radioactive decay is the process by which an unstable atomic nucleus loses energy by radiation.
Three of the most common types are alpha, beta and gamma decay, and when a decay changes the number of protons, an atom of a different element is created.
Decay is random for one atom, yet a large number of identical atoms follow an overall decay rate that can be expressed as a half-life.

facts.label: Discovered
facts.value: By Henri Becquerel in 1896, working with phosphorescent materials

facts.label: Named by
facts.value: Marie and Pierre Curie coined the term radioactivity

facts.label: New elements
facts.value: The Curies isolated polonium and radium

facts.label: Natural radioactive elements
facts.value: 28 on Earth, made up of 35 primordial radionuclides

facts.label: Half-life range
facts.value: From nearly instantaneous to far longer than the universe's age

items.prompt: A single radioactive atom has existed for a very long time, and a friend says it must be due to decay soon. What does quantum theory say?

options.label: It is overdue, so it will decay very soon
Its decay time cannot be predicted, however long it has existed
It will decay at a time fixed when it first formed
Its age tells you roughly when it will decay

items.explain: Radioactive decay is random for single atoms, and it is impossible to predict when a particular atom will decay regardless of how long it has existed.

items.prompt: Nobody can say when one given atom will decay, yet labs report dependable decay rates for samples. How is that possible?

options.label: Labs time each atom and then average the results by hand
Instruments can force each atom to decay at a set moment
For a large number of identical atoms, the overall rate can be expressed as a half-life
The rates are guesses that happen to match most experiments

items.explain: For a significant number of identical atoms, the overall decay rate can be expressed as a decay constant or as a half-life, even though single decays are unpredictable.

items.prompt: After a decay changes the number of protons in a nucleus, what is now true of the atom?

options.label: It has become an atom of a different chemical element
It is the same element with a different mass
It has stopped being radioactive for good
It is the same element in a new physical state

items.explain: Most decays are a nuclear transmutation, and when the number of protons changes, an atom of a different chemical element is created.

items.prompt: Becquerel set many phosphorescent salts on a photographic plate wrapped in black paper. Only one kind blackened the plate. Which?

options.label: Salts that glowed the brightest in the dark
Salts that had sat the longest in strong light
Salts that had been warmed before the test
Uranium salts

items.explain: All results were negative until he used uranium salts, which blackened the plate despite the black paper.

items.prompt: Elster and Geitel ruled out air and outer space as the energy source of radioactivity. What did that suggest about atoms?

options.label: Atoms must soak up energy from the ground below them
Atoms never change, so the energy has to come from elsewhere
Atoms must be altered when they give off the rays
Atoms store light and release it again very slowly

items.explain: If the atoms themselves were the source of energy, the seemingly immutable atoms must be altered when emitting the rays.

items.prompt: Marie Curie studied the radiation from uranium compounds. What did she show about it?

options.label: It was a property of atoms
It was made by the photographic plate itself
It was ordinary X-rays made with electricity
It was sunlight that the compounds had stored

items.explain: Curie named the radiation Becquerel Rays and showed that these rays were a property of atoms, whereas X-rays were produced using electrical energy.
